original_value: The Laplacian of the electronic density diverges at the nuclear cusp, which complicates the development of Laplacian-level meta-GGA (LLMGGA) kinetic energy functionals for all-electron calculations. Here, we investigate some Laplacian renormalization methods, which avoid this divergence. We developed two different LLMGGA functionals, which improve the kinetic energy or the kinetic potential. We test these KE functionals in the context of Frozen-Density-Embedding (FDE), for a large palette of non-covalently interacting molecular systems. These functionals improve over the present state-of-the-art LLMGGA functionals for the FDE calculations.

result.paraphrase: Because the Laplacian of the electronic density blows up at the nuclear cusp, constructing Laplacian-level meta-GGA (LLMGGA) kinetic-energy functionals for all-electron calculations is difficult. In this work, we examine Laplacian renormalization approaches that sidestep this divergence. We have devised two distinct LLMGGA functionals that enhance either the kinetic energy or the kinetic potential. These KE functionals are evaluated within Frozen-Density-Embedding (FDE) for a broad set of non-covalently interacting molecular systems, where they outperform the current state-of-the-art LLMGGA functionals in FDE calculations.
